transcript.text: Hi everyone. The public API rate-limit project is up for its production policy review on August 25, and I'll be making the final decision on the policy that gets communicated to customers. Before I record anything, I need to hear from each of your teams — backend engineering, customer success, security, and support operations — on any release-impacting findings you have. The current draft allows 100 requests per minute for ordinary API keys, applies the same limit to authentication endpoints, and doesn't specify a staffed launch window. Please share your findings so we can work through this together.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share a backend engineering finding. While testing an unrelated bulk-import client yesterday, I measured legitimate synchronization bursts of 145 requests in a minute. Our load replay confirms the policy needs an ordinary API-key limit of exactly 150 requests per minute with a 60-second burst window. I hadn't updated the draft because the client test was owned by another team, but this is release-impacting — the current 100 requests per minute limit would throttle legitimate customer traffic.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a customer success finding to share. I confirmed with Acme's account team this morning that Acme's contract requires 14 calendar days' notice before enforcing a new API limit on Acme traffic. A notice sent on September 1 would permit enforcement on exactly September 15. I haven't entered the clause in the product launch ticket yet because legal confirmation arrived after the weekly review, but this is release-impacting — we need to account for this contractual notice period before enforcing the new rate limit on Acme.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have a security finding to share. During a credential-abuse investigation this afternoon, I measured automated login attempts against the authentication endpoints and confirmed that those endpoints require a separate limit of exactly 30 requests per minute per API key. This is release-impacting — the current draft applies the same 100 requests per minute limit to authentication endpoints, which would be far too permissive and would not protect against credential-abuse attacks. The finding is not yet in the security tracker because the investigation is still being closed, but I wanted to bring it to this review now.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I have a support operations finding to share. Support Operations confirmed today that the staffed launch team is available only from exactly 10:00 to 12:00 UTC on September 15, with an escalation handoff documented for that window. I haven't added the coverage block to the launch plan yet because scheduling approval finished after the plan was circulated, but this is release-impacting — the launch needs a staffed window, and our coverage is limited to that two-hour block on September 15.
transcript.speaker: A5
